title: How a Swarm Chooses a Home

The rest of the bees stay in the old home. The queen and her workers stay close to each other. They hang from a branch close by. The mass of bees is about as big as a football. For now, the branch is just a place to rest. It is not their new home. The bees have only a few days of honey in their guts. They must soon find a dry, safe hole not far away. The new home must have room for the young and for food. There they can make wax cells for their young and store food for winter.
